$comment: Anything not enumerated in `permitted_fields` is DROPPED AT INGEST, before
it is ever persisted. This file is the single source of truth for what the
system is allowed to hold; docs/NOTICE.md is generated FROM this file, so
the employee-facing notice cannot drift from reality.
Per the Phase 2 rule -- if you cannot write the benign explanation, the
field does not ship -- these seed the feature registry rather than being
Reviewed by: engineering. MUST be re-reviewed by counsel + any works
council before this system processes a real person's data.

name.rationale: Identity, required to route a briefing to the right manager conversation.
name.benign_explanation: n/a -- identifier, not a behavioural signal.
name.note: Replaced by a surrogate ID at ingest; the mapping lives in a separate store.

week_number.rationale: Time index. Required for point-in-time correctness and trailing baselines.

tasks_completed.rationale: Throughput relative to the individual's OWN trailing baseline. A sustained personal drop is a prompt to ask what changed.
tasks_completed.benign_explanation: Task size varies enormously. One large architectural task, a research spike, or a shift to mentoring/review work all reduce raw counts while contribution rises.

avg_response_time.rationale: Response latency drift vs the individual's own baseline; a cadence signal, not a productivity one.
avg_response_time.benign_explanation: Deep-focus work, timezone shifts, meeting-heavy weeks, or a deliberate move away from reactive interrupt-driven work all raise latency.

weekly_hours.rationale: Deviation from the individual's own norm, in EITHER direction -- a sustained rise is a burnout prompt, a sustained fall a disengagement prompt.
weekly_hours.benign_explanation: Approved part-time or compressed schedules, phased return from leave, public holidays, and caregiving arrangements all reduce hours legitimately.
weekly_hours.constraint: Absolute thresholds are forbidden. Must be expressed as personal deviation only -- an absolute floor penalises part-time and phased-return workers.

after_hours_logins.rationale: Retained ONLY as a wellbeing/burnout indicator. Structurally barred from raising retention risk.
after_hours_logins.benign_explanation: Non-US timezones, caregivers working after a school run, and personal preference for evening focus time all produce after-hours activity with zero disengagement meaning.
after_hours_logins.constraint: May only ever LOWER concern or trigger a workload check-in. Must never increase a retention-risk score. Triggers US state electronic-monitoring notice duties (NY/CT/DE).

sick_days.reason: HEALTH DATA. GDPR Art. 9 special category; ADA/FMLA discrimination exposure in the US. Using absence to raise a retention-risk score is indefensible.

sentiment.reason: Provenance undocumented. If derived from message content this is an EU AI Act Art. 5 PROHIBITED practice (emotion inference in the workplace) -- banned outright, not merely high-risk. If it is a manager's manual tag it is the circular, bias-contaminated label problem instead.
sentiment.reinstatement_condition: Only with documented provenance proving it is neither content-derived nor a manager opinion, plus counsel sign-off.

task_accuracy.reason: Performance/quality metric. Mixing performance into a retention-support tool is the fastest route to it being used punitively -- the exact failure mode this system is designed to prevent.

forbidden_patterns.$comment: Substring patterns matched case-insensitively against EVERY incoming field name, so a new source cannot introduce a forbidden field simply by not being on the excluded list. Default-deny already blocks these; this exists to make the violation LOUD rather than silent.

retention_days.$comment: TTLs are enforced by src/governance/retention.py and verified by a test that asserts real deletion, not tombstoning.
